summary: Stevens County summit with a 1941 crow's nest, listed abandoned. No source describes the summit today or whether visitors can reach it.

facts.status_note: Listed as abandoned; no source says what, if anything, remains on the summit.

events.note: Crow's nest recorded on the summit

evidence.supports: about nine miles northeast of Chewelah
crow's nest on the summit in 1941
evidence.quote: In 1941, this summit had a crow's nest.

evidence.supports: Stevens County; Pastmaps places the peak at the meeting point of the Kaniksu and Colville forest lines
evidence.quote: Goddards Peak rises above a high-country landscape where the boundaries of the Kaniksu National Forest and Colville National Forest converge in Stevens County.

evidence.supports: Kresek inventory records the crow's nest as abandoned
evidence.quote: The Kresek inventory says it was abandoned.
Hiking Distance: Have not done yet

evidence.supports: a 1964 USGS map on the same page marks a trail climbing to the summit
evidence.quote: 1964 USGS showing trail to top of Goddards Peak

evidence.supports: FFLA list types the site as abandoned

corrections.why: Both lists say abandoned. No source says the structure is gone.
The Forest Fire Lookout Association list types this site as Crowsnest, and firelookout.com and Willhite both describe a crow's nest.

sources.title: 1964 Map of Goddards Peak, Stevens County, WA

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one dated event (1941 crow's nest); the abandonment has no date. The Pastmaps description of the 1964 USGS map mentions a Lookout Tower and a Radio Tower atop Chewelah Mtn, not on Goddards Peak; do not conflate them. Agency: firelookout.com and the record say Colville National Forest; Pastmaps places the peak where the Kaniksu and Colville boundaries meet, so agency is not a true conflict. Willhite gives a 5,548 ft lookout elevation and no hiking distance. Nothing on staffing or fires. No source describes the summit today. Corrections: status gone to abandoned; kind platform to crowsnest.
